sections.html:
West Haven lies in Weber County about 35 miles north of Salt Lake City, with Ogden on its eastern border and Roy to the south. Hooper is to the west and Marriott-Slaterville to the north. It is part of the Ogden-Clearfield metro area, and many residents drive to jobs in Ogden, Roy and Davis County.

The city was formed on July 1, 1991, when the communities of Kanesville and Wilson combined. A citywide sewer system went in during 2002, and that opened the door to denser building. Population climbed from 3,976 in 2000 to 10,272 in 2010 and 16,739 in 2020, and it now stands near 25,627. In 2020 the city had 5,733 housing units with only 5.1% vacant, and homeowner vacancy was 0.7%, so empty houses are rare.

Farmhouses, older grid streets and new subdivisions share the same city limits, which is why two West Haven houses can sell in very different ways.

sections.h2: Winter wear on a house near Ogden
sections.html:
The four seasons are real here. Nearby Ogden averages a July high of 91.3 degrees and a January low of 21.2, with about 16.4 inches of precipitation a year. Its record low is minus 23 and its record high is 106. Snow usually starts in late October or early November and lasts until about April.

That swing is hard on a few parts of a house:

  • Roofs and gutters that hold snow and ice.
  • Exposed pipes and sprinkler lines that can freeze.
  • Furnaces, which work hard for half the year.
  • Driveways and flatwork that crack as the ground freezes and thaws.

An inspector will check each one, and a furnace near the end of its life often becomes a bargaining chip for the buyer.

The census calls West Haven fully urban, yet farm character lingers. Neighborhoods are mostly single-family, with condominiums and multifamily buildings being added, alongside 19th-century farmhouses and working farms that raise crops and animals.

The city bought 40 acres for a park in 1994, and it now has playground equipment, sports fields and a historical marker. Plans call for a River Parkway Trail with a fishing bridge and a pedestrian tunnel under 21st Street, linking to the Weber County Centennial Trail.

The mix matters when you price. A house near the new trails reaches families, while a place on a larger rural lot appeals to buyers who want room for animals or outbuildings. Buyers with children will also ask which school the house feeds. Weber School District covers the city, so confirm the boundary with the district before you advertise.

West Haven's Community Development group covers the Building Department, business licensing, code enforcement and emergency management. City offices are at 4150 S 3900 W, and the main line is 801-731-4519.

Before any repair work, ask city staff which permits apply. Ask your title or escrow company what the buyer's lender will want to see.

A short checklist helps before you list:

  • Finished basements, decks and sheds should have permits on file.
  • Open code complaints should be cleared with city code enforcement.
  • Utility accounts, including the West Haven Special Service District bill, should be current.

sections.h2: How Weber County property tax works
sections.html:
Weber County sends one property tax bill a year, due November 30. Valuation notices go out around July 20, the deadline to appeal your value is September 15, and tax notices follow in mid-October. Anything unpaid turns delinquent on December 1, and penalties and interest follow. Interest on the prior year's delinquent balance begins February 1.

Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence, so tax applies to 55% of market value. In this county the home must be the occupant's main home for at least 183 consecutive days in a year, and a tenant's main home can qualify too. Nightly rentals, vacation homes and second homes cannot. If the county mails you a declaration form and you do not send it back within 30 days, the exemption is dropped. Call the Assessor at (801) 399-8572 if you are unsure where you stand.

At closing the title company divides the year's tax between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Weber County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Weber County Recorder, 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 370, Ogden. The current fee is $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages, and $2.00 for each description over ten.

Out-of-state heirs should expect to sort out the deed and its recording first, before any buyer can close. Your title company can tell you which documents the Recorder wants.

You can list with an agent, sell on your own or ask for a cash offer. Which fits depends on the condition of the house and how much time you have. The roof and the heating system usually drive what a buyer will pay.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Utah houses as they stand. People who call us typically need to move fast because of a job change, an inherited house, a tenant they want to be done with or a mortgage that is behind. We look at the property and explain what a sale would involve, and you choose whether to go ahead.

sections.h2: What West Haven sellers often face
sections.html:
• Competition from new houses in a city that grew by tens of percent in a few years.
  • Older farmhouses and rural lots, where land and house are valued separately.
  • Questions about the primary residence exemption when a house becomes a rental.
  • Out-of-state heirs who must settle a deed before anything else.

An unpaid Weber County bill does not block a sale. The balance, including any penalty and interest, is paid from your proceeds at closing, so ask the Treasurer for a current payoff before you set a closing date. If your house was a rental that you are now selling, check with the Assessor whether the primary residence exemption still applies, because a lost exemption raises the taxable value to the full amount.

Open code complaints and unpaid utility bills can also slow a closing, so settle them first.

sections.h2: What happens once you say yes
sections.html:
If you accept an offer, a title or escrow company takes over the paperwork. It asks Weber County for the tax balance, works out the split of the year's tax, prepares the deed and files it with the Recorder in Ogden. You sign, the funds are sent, and the house is no longer yours to maintain.

Have your deed, your newest tax notice and any permit records on hand. If a mortgage is open, the payoff comes out of the proceeds. If an heir is selling, the title company will say which documents prove the right to sign.

faqs.q: What county is West Haven, UT in?
faqs.a: Weber County. Property tax, deeds and valuation appeals all go through county offices in Ogden.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in West Haven?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on December 1, and interest on the prior year's delinquent balance starts February 1.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Weber County?
faqs.a: The Recorder charges $45.00 for the first page, nothing for additional standard pages and $2.00 for each legal description over ten.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Haven?
faqs.a: The Weber School District. Elementary schools nearby include Country View, Haven Bay, Kanesville and West Haven, and the city has Rocky Mountain and Mountain View junior highs.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Nothing requires you to fix a house before selling, and a cash buyer who accepts the property in its present condition lets you skip repairs.
